game: ATL@IND Week 10 2025, kickoff 2025-11-09 09:30 ET, IND -6.5, total 48.5, roof closed, implied IND 27.5 / ATL 21.0

script.base: Roof closed, moderate 48.5. IND leads by about a score and closes with Jonathan Taylor (42 carries, 292 yards in weeks 7-9) while Daniel Jones still has to throw enough to support a 27.5 team total, with Michael Pittman (30 targets, 268 yards) as the first read. ATL at +6.5 and a 21.0 implied total trails and throws more to Kyle Pitts (26 targets) and Drake London (24 targets, 253 air yards) than it hands to Tyler Allgeier (10 carries, 26 yards).
script.flip1: ATL hangs around or leads because IND is without DeForest Buckner, Samson Ebukam and Tyquan Lewis and only blitzes 27% (Michael Penix Jr. is -0.15 EPA/db vs blitz and +0.05 vs no blitz). Taylor never gets the fourth-quarter carry pile, and both passing games stay live.
script.flip2: IND scores early and leads by 14-plus. Taylor runs the clock, Pittman and Alec Pierce late targets stall, and ATL abandons the run so Bijan Robinson (35 carries, 111 yards, 3.17 YPC in weeks 7-9) and Allgeier rush lines die while London and Pitts targets spike.

injury_fallout: Known pre-kick from the nflverse injury report only; final inactives about 90 minutes before kick are not in the pack. IND DL is gutted: Buckner (neck), Ebukam (knee) and Tyquan Lewis (groin) are Out, so ATL rush efficiency and Penix's time to throw should be better than the weeks 7-9 line, and IND's 27% blitz is even less likely to get home. Anthony Gould (WR, knee) is Out but is not in the weeks 7-9 target list (Pittman 30, Pierce 28, Tyler Warren 17, Josh Downs 12), so no real same-position sleeper bump. ATL: Leonard Floyd (LB, hamstring) Out weakens edge set and a 45% blitz; Storm Norton (T) and Matthew Bergeron (G) Out, Chris Lindstrom (G, foot) Questionable, so ATL protection and rush efficiency are at risk if Lindstrom sits. Mike Hughes (CB, neck) and LaCale London (DT, shoulder) are Questionable, not Out. No IND skill-position starter is Out. Taylor and Pittman are not on the report.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, so MOFO/MOFC and man/zone are unknown. Proxy: IND blitz 27% with the edge rushers out; ATL blitz 45% with Floyd out. Penix is worse when blitzed (-0.15 vs +0.05). Jones is fine when blitzed (+0.13 EPA/db vs +0.22 when not).
matchup.pressure: IND pressure should be down (Buckner, Ebukam, Lewis Out; 27% blitz). That helps ATL intermediate and deep timing and cuts forced checkdowns to Bijan (21 targets, only 28 air yards). ATL pressure should be down with Floyd Out despite the 45% blitz rate, which helps Jones stay on schedule to Pittman. ATL OL losses (Bergeron, Norton Out; Lindstrom Questionable) are the counter for Penix, not for Jones.
matchup.bleeds: ATL run defense: 4.55 YPC and 25 runs of 10+ in 8 games. ATL pass: middle 9.93 YPA but only 42 attempts; right side is the strength at 4.97 YPA on 88 attempts; only 14 passes of 20+ for 233 yards, so they have not been giving up bombs. IND run defense 4.03 YPC but the starting front is out. IND pass: 28 plays of 20+ for 372 yards in 9 games; YPA left 7.61 on 113 attempts, middle 7.26 on 70, right 6.18 on 163.
matchup.overlap: Pittman (240 air yards on 30 targets, about 8.0 aDOT, 268 yards) attacks ATL's middle bleed and does not need the 20+ plays ATL suppresses. Taylor's carry share (42 of 55 listed IND rushes in weeks 7-9) overlaps the 4.55 YPC / 25 explosive-run Falcon front, softer again if Floyd sits and if LaCale London is limited. Pierce (603 air yards, 21.5 aDOT) attacks the explosive area ATL has not bled, so he is not a leg despite 282 yards in three games. London's 253 air yards would overlap IND's 28 explosives, but weeks 7-9 yards are 160 (53.3 per game) against a 55.5 line, so that overlap is not a priced edge.

form: Use weeks 7-9, not season averages. IND: Taylor 42/292 rush and 7/71 receiving; Pittman 30/268/240; Pierce 28/282/603; Warren 17/148 (49.3 per game); Downs 12/89 (29.7). ATL: Bijan 35/111 rush and 21/125 receiving; Allgeier 10/26; Pitts 26/159; London 24/160; Mooney 11/94 on 251 air yards. Prop-card last4 does not subset to those three-game sums for London, Pitts, Downs and others, so last4 is a conflict flag, not a second official window. Where they can be used: Pittman last4 20, 58, 95, 115 (mean 72, two clears of 58.5); Taylor rush last4 123, 94, 153, 45 (mean 103.8, two clears of 94.5, one 45 dud). Pierce's heater is noted and not bet because it is an averages leg into a defense that has allowed 14 explosives in 8 games.

pro_edge.script_read: Favorite 27.5 on a 6.5 spread is a lead-and-run lean for Taylor, not a 14-point blowout, so starter snap risk is only the late-clock case. Underdog ATL should throw more if trailing, which lifts Pitts/London/Bijan targets and cuts Bijan and Allgeier carries. Total 48.5 is neither a shootout nor a slog. Dome, roof closed, so no weather drag on volume.

pro_edge.lagging: No book lines to compare to consensus and no saved move after the spread or total. Stand-in lines are season-to-date medians, so they lag a role change by construction. Clearest lag: Pittman weeks 7-9 at 89.3 yards per game vs the 58.5 median line. Taylor 97.3 vs 94.5 is not a lag.
pro_edge.sleepers: Out: ATL Floyd, Norton, Bergeron; IND Buckner, Ebukam, Lewis, Gould. Questionable (not sleepers): Hughes, Lindstrom, LaCale London. Gould is absent from the weeks 7-9 target list, so Pittman/Pierce/Downs show no same-position line move to shop. No CSV diff. IND DL outs are a matchup note for ATL offense, not a priced sleeper.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. IND led early, Atlanta loaded the box, Taylor finished in the 45-70 range because 6.95 YPC was a three-game heater and 4.55 YPC allowed is only mildly soft, and LaCale London played so the Floyd absence did not open the edge. Pittman posted another 20-40 yard line because the middle 9.93 YPA is 42 throws all year, Hughes played and sat on him, and the fourth quarter was Taylor and the clock. The season-median stand-ins were the right prices, and with no sharp number there was never a proven price edge.
slip_story: One story: IND moderate control in a dome, ahead but not a blowout. Taylor rush over is the lead-and-clock piece; Pittman rec over is the first-read volume still required to reach 27.5. They fail in opposite tails, so this is a 7-10 point win stack, not a parlay with an ATL rush over, a Pierce bomb over, or a game under. No TDs, one market per player, no bet placed.
